name: Bernardo Faria Omoplata System
description: Study Bernardo Faria omoplata entries and defensive reactions with a focused course guide, connected guard positions and clear submission-versus-sweep decisions.
summary: The Bernardo Faria Omoplata System is a BJJGraph study framework for connecting omoplata entries with control, defensive-reaction recognition and the choice between attacking and taking top position.
overview:
Omoplata Everyone offers a focused instructional destination for this shoulder-lock family. Its contents include gi-grip entries, standing and rolling reactions, related attacks and the decision to give up the submission for a positional result. The title is the course name, not a promise that an omoplata will work on every opponent.

BJJGraph's original plan below begins with a closed-guard entry and treats the resulting control as its own skill. A defender standing, rolling or connecting their hands presents a different problem each time. Practise identifying those reactions before choosing a response, and keep a sweep or guard-recovery option available when the original attack no longer fits.
key_principles: Treat entry and retained omoplata control as different stages.
Track the defender's posture before selecting the next response.
Recognise the role of sleeve, belt or lapel grips in a chosen gi setup.
Distinguish maintaining a shoulder attack from accepting a positional result.
Compare standing and rolling reactions in separate drills.
Use controlled movement and release shoulder-lock pressure immediately on a partner signal.

key_components.description: Select a sleeve-based entry and identify the point at which the arm is captured in the intended omoplata configuration.
key_components.purpose: Create a familiar starting sequence for the study plan.

key_components.description: Observe whether the defender remains low or begins to stand and identify how that changes the available connection.
key_components.purpose: Choose a response based on posture rather than a memorised continuation.

key_components.description: Compare a controlled rolling response with a joined-hands defence without assuming they require the same answer.
key_components.purpose: Separate distinct obstacles to continued shoulder control.

key_components.description: Assess when keeping the attack is useful and when accepting top position gives a clearer outcome.
key_components.purpose: Make the positional branch an intentional part of the system.

implementation_sequence.description: Start with the closed-guard sleeve-grip lesson. Note which fabric controls are essential and stop at the intended omoplata position.
Have the partner make a small posture adjustment without rolling. Observe whether the arm remains captured before considering the finish.
Review the relevant section with a coach and practise recognising the posture change without forcing shoulder pressure.
Use a separate cooperative round with an agreed roll and endpoint. Determine whether the attack can be retained or whether a positional result is available.
Repeat the original entry with one of the two agreed reactions. State whether the next goal is continued control, top position or guard recovery.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The entry depends on a sleeve grip that the student has not established.
common_obstacles.solution: Rebuild the entry from its actual grip requirements before opening guard.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Standing and rolling defences are treated as the same reaction.
common_obstacles.solution: Practise them in separate rounds and name the change before responding.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The attacker retains a shoulder lock while the partner rolls unpredictably.
common_obstacles.solution: Reset and use a cooperative, coach-approved rolling drill with no finishing pressure.

common_obstacles.obstacle: A useful sweep is declined because the original submission did not finish.
common_obstacles.solution: Review the positional result as a legitimate branch and practise stabilising top position.

assessment_metrics.description: Assess the relationship between the gi grip and the initial capture.
Identify the defender's chosen posture change.
Check what remains after a defensive movement.
Review the chosen goal after the reaction.
proficiency_indicators: Can retain the attack when appropriate

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph suggests a closed-guard entry followed by two separate reaction rounds. In the first, the partner begins a slow standing response; in the second, use a coach-approved cooperative roll with a clear stopping point. Apply no finishing pressure during the comparison. Name whether the next objective is retained control, a positional result or guard recovery.

progression_path.focus: Establish the sleeve-based capture from closed guard.
Compare a cooperative roll with a fixed endpoint.
Select continued attack, top position or guard recovery from the observed reaction.

common_mistakes: Skipping the gi grips needed for the chosen entry.
Forcing the same response against standing and rolling defences.
Treating a sweep as a failed submission instead of a useful outcome.

flashcards.question: Why record the gi grips used in an omoplata entry?
flashcards.answer: Sleeve, belt or lapel controls may be essential to the chosen setup, so removing them changes the entry and its available control.

flashcards.question: What should be identified before responding to an omoplata defence?
flashcards.answer: Name whether the defender is standing, rolling or connecting their hands, because these are different control problems.

flashcards.question: Why stop an early omoplata drill at control rather than a finish?
flashcards.answer: It allows both partners to assess the captured arm and posture without using shoulder-lock pressure to conceal an unstable entry.

flashcards.question: How should a rolling defence be introduced?
flashcards.answer: Use a cooperative, coach-approved movement with a clear endpoint and no finishing pressure while the positional response is being learned.

flashcards.question: When is taking top position a useful omoplata outcome?
flashcards.answer: It is useful when the reaction offers a stable positional result and continuing the shoulder attack would require chasing lost control.

flashcards.question: Does the course title mean the omoplata is guaranteed to work?
flashcards.answer: No. It is the vendor's course title; the study plan treats control, defensive reactions and positional alternatives as conditional decisions.

products.title: Omoplata Everyone
products.blurb: An omoplata-focused course with gi entries, standing and rolling defences, and a positional branch when the finish is unavailable.
products.best_for: Gi students who already know a basic omoplata and want reaction-specific troubleshooting; several setups depend on fabric grips.
products.study_focus: Start with the closed-guard sleeve entry, then compare standing reactions with the later rolling-defence and positional-result sections.
products.practice_tip: BJJGraph suggestion: separate standing and rolling response rounds and name whether your next objective is control or top position.
